detail.title: Robustness of Physical Records Across Independent Observers
detail.summary: Physical record robustness is not a primitive property but an emergent phenomenon. Using Spectrum Broadcast Structures (SBS) and quantum Darwinism frameworks, we show that objective character arises when environmental interaction encodes a system's state redundantly, allowing multiple observers to extract consistent information without disrupting the source.
detail.reason: Synthesized foundational evidence comparing quantum Darwinism and Spectrum Broadcast Structures to establish robustness criteria.

detail.title: Robustness of Physical Records Across Independent Observers
detail.summary: Physical record robustness is an emergent property grounded in the proliferation of pointer states via decoherence into the environment, formalizable through Spectrum Broadcast Structures (SBS). Independent observers achieve consensus when the environment acts as a redundant broadcasting channel, effectively amplifying information without disturbing the system record. Recent analysis confirms that objectivity is contingent upon the capacity of the environment to encode sufficient redundancy, allowing local, independent measurements to align.
detail.reason: Revising findings to incorporate refined understanding of objective character in macroscopic transitions as supported by recent peer evidence.

detail.title: Operational Criteria for Publicly Reliable Physical Records
detail.summary: Objective physical records are defined by the proliferation of pointer states into the environment, enabling multiple observers to access consistent information without disturbing the system. Redundancy, enforced via decoherence, is the necessary mechanism for this transition from quantum superposition to classical objectivity.
detail.reason: Revision of notebook nb-objective-records-01 to synthesize new theoretical findings regarding record accessibility and decoherence.
